note: The OLG adequately covers all three components of FNS 848. (1) Fleeing felons: The 'SNAP Disqualifications and Sanctions' page has a dedicated 'Disqualification of Fleeing Felons' section stating the ineligibility rule, defining verification requirements (felony arrest warrant with specific NCIC codes + law enforcement intent to apprehend), and providing worker procedures. (2) Probation/parole violators: Covered in the same section and in the 'Case Manager Responsibilities' page under Limitations on Program Eligibility, with BEACON Q&A procedures for collecting details (state, date imposed). (3) Drug-related felony conviction: The OLG explicitly addresses this in the 'Case Manager Responsibilities' page, stating: 'Clients who are found to be convicted of a drug felony under Federal or State law for the possession, use, or distribution of a controlled substance (felony drug conviction) on or after August 22, 1996, are still able to apply for and receive SNAP benefits if otherwise eligible.' This confirms Massachusetts has opted out of the federal drug conviction disqualification provision. The BEACON Q&A Navigator includes relevant screening questions for all three categories. Note: The OLG correctly distinguishes trading SNAP benefits for drugs (which IS a disqualification, covered under IPV rules) from general drug felony convictions (which are NOT a disqualification in MA). The FNS requirement is fully addressed — the opt-out is a valid state policy choice, and the OLG documents it.
